newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes end higher, traders sidelined.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes end higher, traders sidelined.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices ended higher Wednesday, with Alaskan crude tracking benchmark NYMEX amid an absense of local spot trade, dealers said.

The loading of oil tankers got back up to speed at Alaska's Valdez port after a water treatment plant re-opened early Wednesday. When closed, the facility prevented ships from discharging oily ballast water and reduced their capacity to carry out crude for several days.
"I don't see it doing anything to (Alaska North Slope crude) prices," a buyer said.
"It could create some shortages right now...but ultimately it builds inventories," he said, referring to the backup of crude at the port's storage terminals.
Trade was quiet as buyers and sellers waited to see how quickly loadings returned.
A key seller declined to offer a price for ANS and with no sales reported, the ANS discount remained $1.53 below benchmark grade West Texas Intermediate.
Outright ANS prices finished the day 85 cents a barrel over Tuesday levels, in line with the rise on NYMEX.
No deals were reported for California heavy crudes, but outright prices rose in line with the increase in posted prices overnight.
